entries.claim: The standalone editor reproduces first-block loss after save and reload; the baseline has five failing checks and one passing reset-isolation check.
The correct patch passes all six browser checks, while the misleading rerender patch retains the save-and-reload defect.
A recorded seed creates a fresh randomized editor document that is held out from the fixed reproduction cases and checked against each patch.
The acceptance test runs outside the app copies that a repair may modify.
Each local control uses a separate temporary working copy; this local arrangement is not a security sandbox for untrusted code.
An E2B experiment can fork the prepared running environment with the intended filesystem and memory state, and writes remain independent between branches.
An E2B prepared environment can be paused and resumed with the process state required by the experiment, with client reconnection recorded.
Daytona container filesystem snapshots and VM memory snapshots have distinct capture and restore behavior in the selected sandbox classes.
Daytona volume reuse and warm-pool reuse are tested as separate configurations with their matching constraints and costs recorded.
When the deployment advertises filesystem forking, MainBrella's native POST /containers/fork path is exercised and its preserved state is recorded.
In a production MainBrella deployment that lacks native forking, saved-workspace restore is measured as a separate fresh-process path, without describing it as memory preservation.
An external browser context independently reproduces the same user interaction against each provider preview.
A job remains discoverable and its output and final state can be recovered after the review browser disconnects during execution.
Exported diffs, test output, screenshots, and run records remain readable after finished sandboxes are deleted, while expired previews are identified as unavailable.
Comparable provider timings and compute costs are measured with preparation mode, resource allocation, region, reuse, and idle capacity recorded; model cost is reported separately.
Independent repair attempts use the same pinned agent/model configuration, prompt, and budget, and their diffs and verifier outcomes are reported accurately.
A human reviews the selected candidate and approves any pull-request publication.
The workflow generalizes from the planted fixture to a genuinely unresolved bug in an unrelated public repository.

In the local MainBrella run, one saved workspace restored into three independent branches with the prepared filesystem and dependencies intact; writes remained isolated, and each service process had to be started anew.

The unchanged external browser verifier checked protected local MainBrella previews for baseline, correct-repair, and misleading-repair branches, reproducing the expected baseline and misleading failures and confirming all six correct-repair checks.
After the review browser disconnected during a running local managed job, a new browser recovered the same execution ID, exit status, and output without canceling or duplicating the job.

For the local fixture, all four protected previews returned 404 after revocation and after deletion of their exact container generations; API cleanup left no fixture containers or workspaces and zero live reserved workspace bytes, while provider snapshot images remained.
